posts.cooked:
Wow, I do not understand why people seem to get blown up so badly by the V5.

They're a lot like a team of heroes in scope, but with lower average HP, lower average damage, limited ability to focus fire, and no ability to make plans.  Barring really bad luck, why do people have such trouble cleaning their clocks on non-Advanced?

(For anyone who wants to know, I have played two five-Hero games against the V5*, two four-Hero games, one three-Hero game, and two two-Hero games.  I am also basing my opinions on the two five-Hero games against them on the BGG forums.)

As for the original topic, I really like the V5's playstyle, and would very much like to see some V5-compatible promo decks.  That said, I neither expect nor particularly want it to become the new default mode.  Variety is good!

And it is in the name of variety that I am working on a few variant rules to help people out if they want some new faces to switch up their V5 games a little more...

 

* I will allow that one of my five-hero games didn't tell me much, since it contained a Legacy who drew The Next Evolution, followed by all three copies of Heroic Interception back-to-back.  While the first made me wonder why a team which can expect to often face Legacy is so cripplingly dependant on Melee damage, all the HIs will make a joke of essentially any villain, so the V5 get a pass there.

Sean Patrick Fannon:

What I am looking for is advice, possibly modifications, for playing out a version that isn't just Hate Times Ten.

If you're game for trying modifications, why not take a shot playing against The Vengeful H-1?

The Vengeful Five's real advantages are (1) the fact that it's a different playstyle, and people have trouble adjusting, and (2) the fact that at the start of the game, the V5 are 2-3 turns ahead in terms of card play, so (as with so many villains) you're scrambling to catch up from the word go.  So if you have one fewer of them than of you, you should have the extra resources to close that gap, and so have a better chance to get used to the different target priorities of fighting the V5 before you take on the full set.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
If you have less than 5 players leave out the Baron.

That really helps.

They are really tough, You have to manage the clones or they will kill you, you have to keep Blade from getting too built up, you want to get rid of Frictions devices, and you are getting pounded by Fright Train.

Oh and Ermine would love for you to ignore her.

Bring lots of toughness and damage.

Tempest is great against them, all target damage is good, and we got to a point where we got to use shackles on 4 of them in one attack.

Legacy is big, he can eliminate the Melee damage if you get the right cards, otherwise his damage boosting makes the all target damage really good.

Fanatic is amazing, End of Days is a Godsend when they are flooding the field with cards, first turn EoD is incredible.

Chrono Ranger's bounties are also awesome.

Haka and Rampage, Bunker and External, any all target damage is great.  Also since non-advanced they have almost no armor Hypersonic is awesome.  Ground Pound and Grease Gun are also sick, and Salvage Yard is an awesome combo with Ermine, she feeds your trash, you recover.

 

the big threat is the damage they put out and the total amount of health they make you burn through to win.  Boosting and reducing are big, but since it is so many targets stun bolts and that ilk aren't as good (and better used against all target damage threats than Fright Train)

 

Bring your A-team, because you will need it.  Don't bring heroes that need lots of cards in play to work, but Bunker and Ammo Drop is incredible, so many villain cards to destroy.

I like Legacy, Tempest, Bunker, Fanatic, Ranger, Haka, Fixer.  They all do well vs. the V5.  If you take at least three of them you should have an easier time.

Don't do Atlantis.  Just don't.

posts.name: Ironic
posts.cooked:
Legacy and Tempest are good tech against The Vengeful Five, much as they are against everything else, yeah.

More generally, the V5 win by drowning you in damage before you're set up, like Iron Legacy.  Unlike IL, their damage can be reduced, so a good tank, or someone who can speed setup (hello, Omnitron-X) are strong counters.

posts.name: lynkfox
posts.cooked:
Remember to make use of their weaknesses. Take out Shock Dampners first, but then you can almost (almost) ignore Friction. She'll kill herself. Anytime you have multi target attacks, throw one at Fright Train to get  the extra bonus damage. Blade can certainly wait till last, but that impulsion beam has to go.  Proletariat can certainly become an issue, but if you keep a handle on the clones (Tacyone Hypersonic Assult is great, but removes their drawback, other methods to neuter them are good) you can manage.

 

Its a much trickier game - its much much more about management - its Ennead on Advanced with everyone having a trigger another card play (in effect) or Citizen Dawn on crack. Its possible... just more threat managment than usual.

 

Prioritize, but don't be afraid to adjust priority as the game board changes.
